requirement: VLAN 120を作成し、アクセスポートに割り当てる

section_path: Creating or Modifying an Ethernet VLAN
Assigning Static-Access Ports to a VLAN

assumptions_requiring_confirmation: The request concerns an ordinary Ethernet data VLAN, not a voice, private or remote-SPAN VLAN.
Each command block starts at privileged EXEC mode on the intended switch.
The current device state and VTP configuration permit local VLAN creation.

items.requirement: VLAN 120をスイッチ上に作成する
items.assessment: The source describes VLAN creation and the requested ID is within the normal configurable range. Device prerequisites and an unusual media-setting step still need review.
missing_information: Current VTP version, mode and domain; whether VLANs are centrally managed.
Whether VLAN 120 already exists and what currently uses it.
Applicable device capacity and spanning-tree constraints.

withheld_source_steps.reason: The retrieved procedure lists a media-setting step without an optional marker. Its applicability and whether it may be omitted on this target require PDF/command-reference review; the partial block is not a reproduction of the complete procedure.
The retrieved procedure repeats end in Steps 5 and 6. The duplicate is not presented as a justified additional mode transition.

items.requirement: 物理アクセスポートをVLAN 120に割り当てる
items.assessment: The source directly describes static access-port mode and VLAN assignment, but the target interface is unspecified.
missing_information: Existing interface configuration and whether changing its role is authorized.
Whether the interface belongs to a port channel; the source restricts changes to the port channel when interfaces are bundled.
Confirmation that VLAN 120 is available before assigning the port.

next_checks: Confirm the target interface, current switch configuration and intended VLAN type.
Check the cited procedures and cautions against the original PDF; resolve the media step and repeated end before treating the draft as a complete procedure.
Confirm applicable VTP and port-channel constraints without automatically changing them.
After review, use the cited verification commands to define expected results; no command has been executed on a device.
